title: AffineKummerDegreeOneBaseChange
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth separated connected affine curve [def-sc-curves]. Let $n\geq1$ be nonzero in $k$. Let $\varphi:\pi^{-1}(\mathrm{Kummer}_C)\to\mathrm{Kummer}_{C_K}$ be a morphism of Kummer short complexes [def-sc-kummer-sequence], where $\pi:C_K\to C$ is the projection, and assume its middle component is the comparison on $\mathbf G_m$ induced by pullback of units. Then the map $H^1(\varphi_1)\circ\rho^1(C,\mu_n):H^1(C,\mu_n)\to H^1(C_K,\mu_n)$ is bijective.

source.place: affine-case degree-one paragraph: natural Kummer sequence comparison

proof.text: Obtain the natural short-exact Kummer ladder, the units and Picard equations, and the affine Picard-torsion bijection. Cancel the monic roots-of-unity inclusion to identify the first component of the given morphism with the natural one.

The exact Kummer sequence has maps alpha from additive units and beta to H1(Gm). The kernel of alpha is the subgroup of nth powers; the image of beta is Picard n-torsion. The ladder equations identify pullback on these terms.

The units quotient isomorphism respects representatives. Equality of quotient classes makes alpha-boundaries equal, since their quotient is an nth power. Injectivity reflects zero alpha-boundaries, and surjectivity lifts every target alpha-boundary.

If a middle class maps to zero, its beta-image is zero by torsion injectivity, hence it is an alpha-boundary. Units-quotient injectivity makes that boundary zero. To lift a target middle class, first lift its beta-image using torsion surjectivity and beta exactness. The remaining difference is an alpha-boundary; lift that boundary using the units quotient and add it to the chosen source class.
